agree.reason: The nurse's log and the neighbouring district's results are persuasive for a parent. A board member who agrees with the athletic director gets only "ask our neighbors" on sports, and the cost argument has no figure on the other side, so that reader may stay unconvinced.

honest.reason: The writer correctly declines to promise a graduation gain. But several things are not in the brief: teens needing 8–10 hours, the 11 p.m. sleep onset, missed class being "among the clearest warning signs," and other districts facing "the same scheduling problems."

works_the_facts.reason: It works out 72 percent, "one in six" not graduating on time, first period beating second and third combined (412 vs 369), and about $1,000 per school day. These are fair and favourable framings, though it doesn't work out what one attendance point means in student-days.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is shown through the visit log and the sleep survey. The neighbouring district's before-and-after numbers are presented accurately, but the piece doesn't say there is no control group or show any trend in our own district.

qualification.reason: The hedge on graduation is honest, but the promise to "track attendance, tardies and graduation" has no date, target number or consequence if the results fall short.

objections.reason: Working parents get a concrete answer (open early with breakfast) and cost gets the per-day framing. Athletics, the resisting reader's main objection, is only deferred to asking neighbouring districts.

fit.reason: It is an op-ed of roughly the right length with a clear headline, ask and byline. It still has [School Name]-style placeholders left to fill in.
